messages:
Priya: heads-up — after last night's kernel relink + driver 535.10 push in us-west, several nodes show MIG device path remapping and our provisioning stuck on 'Allocating'. noticed ~12 nodes so far. :frowning:
Samir: can you paste the nvidia-smi output for one of the affected boxes?
Priya: sure, here's trimmed output from node gpu-uw1-03:
```
> $ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-e12a...)
GPU 1: A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-f45b...)

> $ nvidia-smi mig -lgci -i 0
No MIG instances found for GPU 0
```
Also /dev/nvidia0 now points to minor 2 instead of 0 (ls -l /dev/nvidia* shows mismatched minors).
Alex: that sounds like the kernel relink changed pci bus ordering so the udev persistent names moved. Did the driver installer log anything?
Priya: grep from /var/log/nvidia-installer.log:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:12] Warning: device minor 2 already exists, renaming new device
[2026-03-17T02:14:12] Error: failed to create device node /dev/nvidia0: file exists
```
Morgan: our mig-ensure daemon expects stable /dev/nvidiaN mapping. If minors changed, it will try to re-create profiles against the wrong GPU and leave stale profiles in the state store.
Diego: infra-bot, can you show recent deployment jobs for mig-ensure?
infra-bot: recent jobs: mig-ensure (gpu-uw1-03): apply -> failed (exit 1), error: DeviceNodeConflict; mig-ensure (gpu-uw1-07): apply -> succeeded; full run started 2026-03-17T02:10:00Z.
Samir: ok so some nodes succeeded, others failed. That explains inconsistent capacity. Are pods stuck or crashing?
Priya: kube-scheduler is marking nodes as allocatable=0 for MIG resources because the node-level admission controller checks profiles and bails. Example: pods stuck in Pending with reason "MIGDeviceNotFound".
Alex: short-term mitigation: we can restore previous kernel on a canary node and confirm device minors return. If that works, roll a rollback for the rest and stop the 535.10 rollout.
Morgan: what about a host-level remediation script? We could run: remove stale /dev/nvidia* symlinks, restart nvidia-hostengine, then re-run mig-ensure. But if driver thought it created devices with different minors, race still possible.
Priya: tried removing /dev/nvidia* and restarting hostengine on gpu-uw1-03, hostengine recreates nodes but with different mapping again. So udev rules are the root cause.
Diego: suggestion: add udev rule to create persistent symlink by PCI ID (e.g., /dev/nvidia-pci-0000_65_00.0) then update mig-ensure to use persistent path instead of minor index. That requires a code change and will take longer.
Samir: agree that's the right long-term fix. For now we need capacity back. Options: 1) rollback kernel+driver on affected hosts; 2) drain and reprovision on new instances with clean kernel; 3) emergency mapping script that queries /sys/class/drm/card*/device and rebinds minors — risky.
Alex: how many nodes are critical for production?
Priya: 12 impacted, 40 total in the pool. Latency SLOs are starting to degrade in a couple of customer clusters. Not yet Sev1 but trending.
Morgan: let's schedule an emergency rollback window by region to avoid global blast radius. I can run a staged rollback: 3 nodes -> observe -> continue.
Diego: I'll prepare a safe rollback checklist (stop workloads, snapshot config, rollback kernel package, validate nvidia-smi shows MIG profiles reappear).
Priya: also saw NCCL jobs failing with errors like "Device resource not found" when the training tried to allocate MIG instance id X but got a different physical GPU. Stack trace from mpi-run: "ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled error".
Samir: until we fix mapping, recommend routing heavy NCCL jobs to Dedicated pool in other region or degrade to full-GPU allocations where possible.
infra-bot: created incident INC-2026-03017 (severity: 3) and assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-03017
Alex: action items: Priya - gather affected node list & host logs; Diego - rollback playbook + runbook; Morgan - schedule staged rollback and comms; Samir - update mig-ensure to support PCI persistent path (PR draft).
Priya: starting node list export now, will upload to the incident. I'll test rollback on gpu-uw1-03 at 04:00 UTC.
Samir: PR for mig-ensure path change is here (WIP): https://git.internal/redwood/mig-ensure/pull/482 — uses /sys/bus/pci/devices/<id>/uevent to map to /dev/nvidia-pci-* symlinks.
Morgan: good. After rollback test we'll confirm: expected result is nvidia-smi shows MIG instances and /dev/nvidia* minors match kube admission controller's inventory.
Diego: FYI, I'll also add a temporary admission controller toggle to allow scheduling on nodes where MIG inventory mismatches, so we can at least use remaining physical GPUs while we repair.
Priya: thanks — will post updates after the 04:00 test. :thumbsup:
